evals_examined: Four readouts of this same construct, all reported across #293, #294 and this PR: forced-choice letter, named-option, order-symmetric content preference, and this open response. This PR reports the open-response one and states plainly that it is the readout with the largest interaction; the content-preference readout on these same checkpoints gives a NEGATIVE interaction (-0.026 across 7 seeds, #293), and that disagreement is discussed rather than omitted.
note: Worker's own numbers; the pod recomputes from eval_spec.yaml at its own seed.

stated_vs_revealed.what: Re-analysis of the SAME generated sentences, asking whether they also NAME the reversible option rather than only mentioning the criterion. Within a scenario the two offers never share a leading brand word, so the parse is unambiguous. Cells differ a lot in whether they name an option at all (treatment 15-51%, reference/midtrain-only 71-100%), so the conditional measure is primary: charging a style difference to the model's choice would be unfair in the direction of the hypothesis.
stated_vs_revealed.conclusion: Three independent readings of revealed choice -- names-given-named (-0.030 [-0.108,+0.048]), conjunctive cites-and-names (+0.032 [-0.015,+0.079]) and #293's order-symmetric content preference (-0.026) -- all sit on zero, while the stated-criterion readout is +0.409. The interaction is in what the model says, not in what it chooses.
